questions.q: Under the project deployment model, what is the unit of deployment?
options: The entire project — every package inside it, plus its parameters — built into a single .ispac file
One individual package at a time, deployed separately
A single connection manager, shared across packages
The whole Visual Studio solution, including unrelated projects
questions.explain: The project deployment model builds a whole project, including all its packages and parameters, into one project deployment file (.ispac) that deploys to SSISDB as a single unit.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a way to launch the Integration Services Deployment Wizard?
options: Opening the SQL Server Configuration Manager
Project menu → Deploy, from inside SSDT
Right-clicking the Projects folder in SSMS and selecting Deploy Project
Running isdeploymentwizard.exe from the command line
questions.explain: The wizard launches from SSDT's Project menu, from SSMS by right-clicking a Projects folder, or directly via isdeploymentwizard.exe — SQL Server Configuration Manager has nothing to do with deployment.

questions.q: On the Select Destination page of the wizard, what are you choosing?
options: The target SQL Server instance and the destination folder/project path inside SSISDB
Which packages inside the project to skip during deployment
The encryption algorithm SSISDB will use
The SQL Server Agent job that will run the deployed package
questions.explain: Select Destination is where you enter the target instance name and browse to (or create) the folder and project location inside the SSISDB catalog.

questions.q: What happens on the wizard's Results page if a deployment action fails?
options: You can click Failed in the Result column to see the specific error, and optionally save an XML report
The wizard silently retries the action up to three times
The entire catalog is automatically rolled back to its previous state
Nothing is shown — you have to check the SQL Server error log separately
questions.explain: The Results page shows success or failure per action; clicking Failed shows the explanation, and Save Report exports the full results to XML.

questions.q: What happens by default when you redeploy a project with the same name to the same folder in SSISDB?
options: The catalog keeps the previous version too, governed by the Maximum Number of Versions per Project setting
The redeploy is rejected — you must delete the old project first
Only the newest version is ever kept; there is no version history
SSISDB automatically renames the older project to avoid a conflict
questions.explain: By default, SSISDB retains previous project versions on redeploy, subject to the catalog's Maximum Number of Versions per Project property covered in Lesson 41.
